book: Nancy Caroline · Chapter 12 · Expanded EMS Systems and Community Paramedicine in Canada
title: Community Paramedicine: Expanded Roles and Safe Nontransport

slides.title: Today's lesson
slides.body:
As an EMR you already respond, treat and transport to the ED: traditional scope. Today, as a PCP:

  1. Define community paramedicine, expanded scope and expanded role
  2. See how Canadian programs work, and what they achieved
  3. Understand why nontransport is risky, and what makes it safer

Textbook: Chapter 12, PDF pages 868–906
slides.say: Welcome back. Think about the job you know as an EMR: respond in an ambulance, give emergency care, and take the patient to the emergency department. The textbook calls that traditional scope paramedicine. This chapter is about everything beyond it. Sometimes that means new skills; sometimes it means your existing skills in new places, like homes, clinics and shelters. Today we'll cover three things: the key definitions, real Canadian programs and their results, and the hardest question in this field: when is it safe not to transport, and what must be in place first?
slides.sayZh: 欢迎回来。想想你作为 EMR 熟悉的工作：开着救护车出车，做急救，把病人送到急诊。教材称之为传统范围的院前医学。这一章讲的是它之外的一切。有时这意味着学新技能，有时意味着把已有技能用到新地方，比如病人家里、诊所和收容所。今天讲三件事：关键定义；真实的加拿大项目和它们的成效；以及这个领域最难的问题：什么时候不转运是安全的，之前必须具备什么条件？

slides.title: Expanded scope vs expanded role
slides.body:
Expanded scopeExpanded role
new skills and protocols, beyond original trainingexisting skills, in a nontraditional setting
e.g. suturing, IV antibiotics at homee.g. assessing frail patients at home
  • Community paramedicine: care outside respond-and-transport
  • Differentiated practice: non-urgent work matched to expertise
slides.say: First, the terms. Community paramedicine means paramedics using their training in community settings, outside the usual emergency response and transport model. There are two kinds of expansion. Expanded scope means new skills and protocols beyond your original training, such as suturing or giving IV antibiotics at home. Expanded role means using the skills you already have in a new setting, such as assessing frail patients in their homes. Differentiated practice means using paramedics for nonemergency or non-life-threatening situations, matched to their expertise and qualifications. Memory aid: new skills is scope; old skills in a new place is role.
slides.sayZh: 先讲术语。社区院前医学指救护员在社区环境中运用所学，跳出常规的急救响应和转运模式。扩展有两种。扩展范围是超出原有培训的新技能和新协议，比如缝合、在家输抗生素。扩展角色是把已有技能用到新场景，比如上门评估体弱的病人。分化实践是按救护员的专长和资质，把他们用于非急诊或不危及生命的情况。口诀：新技能是范围，老技能换新地方是角色。

slides.title: Who needs it, and why paramedics?
slides.body:
• Rural and remote towns, often with no family doctor
  • Homeless and underhoused people in cities
  • Long-term care residents and people in prison
  • Determinants of health: food, housing, income, isolation
  • Paramedics are in every community, usually 24/7
slides.say: Who benefits? Poor access isn't only rural, though towns with no family doctor often rely on paramedics. In cities, people who are homeless or underhoused, meaning living in run-down rooms with poor heat or sanitation, often fall through the cracks. So do people in long-term care and in prison. Determinants of health, like housing, income and isolation, matter too. Frail older people can do badly when moved out of their home or community for care. Paramedics are in every community, usually around the clock, so they're well placed to fill these gaps.
slides.sayZh: 谁会受益？可及性差不只是农村的问题，虽然没有家庭医生的小镇常常依赖救护员。在城市里，无家可归者和住房不足者，也就是住在破旧、供暖或卫生条件差的房间里的人，常常被漏掉。长期护理机构的住户和监狱里的人也一样。住房、收入和社会隔绝等健康决定因素也很重要。体弱老人被送离家或社区去就医时，结局可能更差。救护员遍布每一个社区，通常全天候在岗，所以很适合填补这些空缺。

slides.title: The CSA's three program types
slides.body:
Care is differentdialysis support, blood draws, IV antibiotics, clinicsnew services
Response is differentcase finding and referral, early discharge, hybrid 9-1-1new ways to answer calls
Coordination of careremote monitoring, health surveillance, promotionkeeping people connected

Most real programs mix all three: each grows from local needs.
slides.say: A standard from the Canadian Standards Association, or CSA, sorts programs into three types. In the first, the care is different: new services such as dialysis support, blood draws, IV antibiotics, or clinics. In the second, the response is different: finding at-risk people and referring them, helping patients leave hospital early, or hybrid nine-one-one, which means answering some nine-one-one calls in a different way. In the third, the goal is coordinating care: remote monitoring, health surveillance, and health promotion. Most real programs mix all three, because each grows from local needs.
slides.sayZh: 加拿大标准协会，也就是 CSA 的标准，把项目分成三类。第一类，照护不同：提供新服务，比如透析支持、采血、静脉抗生素或诊所。第二类，响应不同：找出高危人群并转介、协助病人提前出院，或者混合 911，也就是用另一种方式应答部分 911 呼叫。第三类，目标是协调照护：远程监测、健康监测和健康促进。实际项目大多三类都有，因为每个项目都是从本地需求里长出来的。

slides.title: Canadian examples
slides.body:
• In hospital: Halifax ED paramedics; collaborative emergency centres
  • Acute care: ECG reading, STEMI diagnosis, fibrinolysis, ECMO activation
  • Alternatives: taxi, walk-in clinic, or a home plan with a doctor
  • Nova Scotia ECPs: nursing-home 9-1-1 calls, care plans
  • Treat and release: e.g. hypoglycemia, opioid overdose, known epilepsy
slides.say: In Halifax, paramedics work in the emergency department under physician oversight, managing airways, suturing and casting. Nova Scotia also replaced some quiet rural EDs with collaborative emergency centres, staffed overnight by a paramedic and a nurse. Others expand acute care: reading ECGs, diagnosing STEMI, giving clot-busting drugs, or activating ECMO teams for selected cardiac arrests. Some offer alternatives to the ED, like a taxi, a walk-in clinic, or a home plan made with a doctor. Nova Scotia's extended care paramedics answer nursing home calls and have greatly reduced ED transports. And some systems treat and release patients by protocol.
slides.sayZh: 在哈利法克斯，救护员在医生监督下在急诊科工作，处理气道、缝合和打石膏。新斯科舍还把一些冷清的农村急诊改成协作急诊中心，夜间由一名救护员和一名护士值守。有的扩展急性照护：判读心电图、诊断 STEMI、给溶栓药，或为部分心脏骤停病人启动 ECMO 团队。有的提供急诊以外的选择，比如出租车、walk-in 诊所，或与医生共同制定的居家方案。新斯科舍的延伸照护救护员应答养老院呼叫，大大减少了送急诊的次数。还有些系统按协议做治疗后放行。

slides.q: A service sends PCPs to a seniors' housing building once a week. Using only skills they already have, they check blood pressure and blood sugar and refer anyone who needs follow-up. How is this best described?
options: Expanded scope: new skills beyond their training
Expanded role: existing skills in a nontraditional setting
slides.say: Let's check the terms. A service sends PCPs to a seniors' housing building once a week. Using only skills they already have, they check blood pressure and blood sugar, and refer anyone who needs follow-up. How is this best described? A, expanded scope: new skills beyond their training. B, expanded role: existing skills in a nontraditional setting. C, traditional scope paramedicine. D, treat and release. Tap your answer.
slides.sayZh: 检查一下术语。某服务每周派 PCP 到一栋老年住宅楼，只用他们已有的技能测血压和血糖，并把需要跟进的人转介出去。最恰当的描述是什么？A 扩展范围：超出培训的新技能；B 扩展角色：已有技能用于非传统场景；C 传统范围院前医学；D 治疗后放行。点选你的答案。
slides.explain: The answer is B, expanded role. The skills are ones the paramedics already have; what's new is the setting, a community clinic instead of an emergency call. It would be expanded scope only if they needed new skills, such as giving IV antibiotics. It isn't traditional scope, because there's no emergency response and no transport. And treat and release means treating an emergency on scene by protocol, then leaving the patient at home.
slides.explainZh: 答案是 B，扩展角色。技能是救护员本来就有的，新的是场景：社区诊所，而不是急救呼叫。只有需要新技能，比如静脉输抗生素，才算扩展范围。它也不是传统范围，因为没有急救响应，也不转运。治疗后放行是指在现场按协议处理一个急症，然后让病人留在家里。

slides.title: What the programs achieved
slides.body:
ProgramReported result
Long and Brier Islands, NSED transports −23%
Renfrew County, ON9-1-1 calls −5.1%; ED transports −23.4%
Toronto CP@Homefrequent callers' 9-1-1 use −32%
Winnipeg EPICEMS transports −42.3%; ED visits −21.9%

Common thread: find high-risk patients → assess at home → refer and coordinate.
slides.say: Do these programs work? On Nova Scotia's Long and Brier Islands, where reaching hospital takes two ferry trips, community paramedics see about two hundred fifty to three hundred patients a month, and ED transports off the islands fell twenty-three percent. In rural Renfrew County, Ontario, program areas saw nine-one-one calls fall about five percent in a year, and ED transports fall over twenty-three percent. Toronto's home visit program cut frequent callers' nine-one-one use by thirty-two percent. Winnipeg's EPIC program cut EMS transports by forty-two percent. The common thread: find high-risk patients early, assess them where they live, then refer and coordinate.
slides.sayZh: 这些项目有用吗？新斯科舍的朗岛和布里尔岛，去医院要坐两趟轮渡；社区救护员每月看大约二百五十到三百人，离岛送急诊减少了百分之二十三。安省农村的伦弗鲁县，有项目的地区一年里 911 呼叫下降约百分之五，送急诊下降超过百分之二十三。多伦多的家访项目让高频呼叫者的 911 使用减少了百分之三十二。温尼伯的 EPIC 项目让 EMS 转运减少了百分之四十二。共同点是：及早找出高危病人，在他们住的地方评估，然后转介和协调。

slides.title: Nontransport: why it's controversial
slides.body:
Deciding a 9-1-1 patient doesn't need the ED is hard and risky

  • Many studies: paramedic-initiated nontransport is overall unsafe
  • Leading cause of EMS lawsuits in the United States
  • Patient may worsen at home, or be too sick to call again
  • Traditional training teaches transport, not screening
slides.say: Crowded EDs make it tempting to have paramedics screen out patients who don't need to go. But deciding that someone who called nine-one-one doesn't need to go is very difficult. Many studies have found paramedic-initiated nontransport overall unsafe, and in the United States it's the leading cause of lawsuits against EMS. Picture leaving a patient at home, and hours later the family calls back because he's much worse. Or nobody calls, because he lives alone and is now too sick to phone. Traditional paramedic training teaches you to transport, not to screen patients out. That gap is where the danger lies.
slides.sayZh: 急诊拥挤，让人很想让救护员筛出不需要去的病人。但要判断一个打了 911 的人不需要去医院，非常困难。许多研究认为救护员发起的不转运总体上不安全；在美国，它是 EMS 被起诉的首要原因。想象一下：你把病人留在家里，几小时后家属又打电话，因为他明显恶化了。或者根本没人打电话，因为他独居，现在病得打不了电话。传统的救护培训教你送病人去医院，而不是把病人筛掉，危险就在这个空白里。

slides.title: What makes nontransport safer
slides.body:
1. Extra training: spot who is high risk at home
  2. Formal protocols: when treat-and-release or an alternative fits
  3. Medical oversight
  4. Quality assurance and patient safety monitoring

Wrong patient left home → complications, longer stays, even ICU admission.
slides.say: So when can nontransport be done safely? First, extra training, so paramedics can spot patients at higher risk if left at home. Second, formal protocols that say exactly when treat and release, or an alternative such as palliative care at home, is appropriate. Third, medical oversight. Fourth, quality assurance and patient safety monitoring, the tools from our last chapter. Without these supports, choosing the wrong patient can mean complications, longer hospital stays, even intensive care.
slides.sayZh: 那么什么时候不转运可以做得安全？第一，额外培训，让救护员能认出留在家里风险更高的病人。第二，正式协议，明确什么时候适合治疗后放行或替代方案，比如居家姑息照护。第三，医疗监督。第四，质量保证和患者安全监测，也就是上一章讲的工具。没有这些支撑，选错病人可能导致并发症、住院延长，甚至进 ICU。

slides.title: Building a program: the CSA steps
slides.body:
Plan→Scope→Stakeholders→Recruit→Train→Sustain
  • Start with a needs assessment
  • Unclear scope → role conflict, scope creep, unmet expectations
  • Partners sign information-sharing agreements (e.g. an MOU)
  • 8 CSA principles, e.g. patient- and family-centred, safety
slides.say: How is a program built? It starts with a needs assessment: what's the gap, and is it a good fit for paramedics? Then the CSA suggests six steps. Write a plan, including risks and how to reduce them. Define the scope: who is served, what care, why, when and where. An unclear scope leads to role conflict, scope creep, which means duties slowly growing beyond the plan, and unmet expectations. Involve stakeholders early, like doctors, hospitals, housing agencies and regulators, with agreements to share information. Then recruit, train, and plan for the long run beyond the pilot. Eight CSA principles guide it, including patient- and family-centred care, and safety.
slides.sayZh: 项目是怎么建起来的？先做需求评估：缺口在哪里？让救护员来填补合不合适？然后 CSA 建议六步。写计划，包括风险和应对办法。界定范围：服务谁、提供什么照护、为什么、何时、何地。范围不清会导致角色冲突、范围蔓延，也就是职责慢慢超出计划，以及期望落空。及早让相关方参与，比如医生、医院、住房机构和监管机构，并签订信息共享协议。然后招聘、培训，并为试点结束后的长期运作做好规划。整个过程由 CSA 八条原则指导，包括以病人和家庭为中心，以及安全。

slides.title: The hidden cost of an ED trip
slides.body:
For a frail older patient, the ED trip itself carries risk

  • Delirium in a strange, noisy place
  • Missed regular medications while waiting
  • Pressure sores from hours on a stretcher
  • → longer admission, worse function than before
  • Where allowed: a shared plan with patient, staff, doctor, oversight
slides.say: For a frail older patient, the trip to the emergency department carries its own risks. Hours in a strange, noisy hallway can trigger delirium, which means sudden confusion and agitation. Regular medications get missed while they wait. Skin breaks down into pressure sores on a stretcher never meant for long stays. The result can be a longer admission and a patient who goes home weaker than before. Where a system has the right structure, the patient, care home staff, the facility doctor and medical oversight can agree on a shared plan. Where it doesn't, transport to the ED may be the only option.
slides.sayZh: 对体弱老人来说，去急诊这一趟本身就有风险。在陌生嘈杂的走廊里待上几个小时，可能诱发谵妄，也就是突然出现的糊涂和烦躁。等候时常规药物会被漏掉。担架本来就不是给人久躺的，皮肤会磨出压疮。结果可能是住院更久，出院时比之前更虚弱。如果系统有合适的架构，病人、护理院员工、机构医生和医疗监督可以商定一个共同方案。如果没有，送急诊可能就是唯一的选择。

slides.q: Your service proposes letting PCPs leave low-acuity 9-1-1 patients at home on crew judgment alone, with no extra training, protocol, or physician oversight. Based on this chapter, what is the best response?
options: Support it: paramedics already know who needs the ED
Raise concerns: it needs training, protocols, medical oversight, QA and safety monitoring
Support it, as long as each patient signs a form
Support it only in rural areas, where transports take longest
slides.say: Here's a PCP decision. Your service proposes letting PCPs leave low-acuity nine-one-one patients at home on crew judgment alone, with no extra training, no protocol, and no physician oversight. Based on this chapter, what's the best response? A, support it; paramedics already know who needs the ED. B, raise concerns; it needs training, protocols, medical oversight, quality assurance and safety monitoring. C, support it, as long as each patient signs a form. D, support it only in rural areas, where transports take longest. Tap your answer.
slides.sayZh: 来做一道 PCP 决策题。你的服务提议：让 PCP 单凭救护组的判断，把低急的 911 病人留在家里，不加额外培训，没有协议，也没有医生监督。根据这一章，最好的回应是什么？A 支持，救护员本来就知道谁需要去急诊；B 提出顾虑：这需要培训、协议、医疗监督、质量保证和安全监测；C 支持，只要每个病人签一张表；D 只在转运时间最长的农村地区支持。点选你的答案。
slides.explain: The answer is B. Studies have found paramedic-initiated nontransport overall unsafe, and traditional training teaches transport, not screening. The textbook says a safe program needs extra training, formal protocols, medical oversight, quality assurance, and patient safety monitoring. A assumes a skill most paramedics were never trained in. C doesn't make the decision safer; a signature can't stop a patient from getting worse. D is wrong because location doesn't remove the risk; the same safeguards are needed everywhere.
slides.explainZh: 答案是 B。研究认为救护员发起的不转运总体上不安全，而传统培训教的是转运，不是筛查。教材说，安全的项目需要额外培训、正式协议、医疗监督、质量保证和患者安全监测。A 假定了大多数救护员从未受过训练的能力。C 并没有让决定更安全，一个签名阻止不了病人恶化。D 错，因为换个地方并不能消除风险，哪里都需要同样的保障。

slides.title: What the PCP actually does
slides.body:
• Follows the protocols your system actually has
  • Never improvises nontransport on scene
  • Spots frail patients and frequent callers who need more support
  • Uses a referral pathway only where one exists
  • Involves medical oversight; documents the reasoning

A community paramedic role needs further formal education.
slides.say: What does this mean for a working PCP? Much of your work will be on a traditional ambulance. You follow the protocols your system actually has; nontransport isn't something you improvise on scene. But you can still think like a community paramedic. Notice the frail older patient who keeps falling, or the caller who phones every week. In Toronto, for example, frontline paramedics refer patients like these to home care through their electronic patient care record. Use a referral pathway only where your system has one. When needs don't fit the usual model, involve medical oversight rather than deciding alone, and document your reasoning. The CSA expects community paramedics to complete further formal, recognized education.
slides.sayZh: 这对在职 PCP 意味着什么？你的大部分工作会在传统救护车上。你遵循系统实际拥有的流程；不转运不是你在现场临时发挥的选项。但你仍然可以像社区救护员一样思考：留意那个反复跌倒的体弱老人，或者每周都打电话的呼叫者。比如在多伦多，一线救护员可以通过电子病人照护记录，把这样的病人转介到居家照护。只有在你的系统有转介途径时才用它。当病人的需求不符合常规模式时，找医疗监督商量，而不是自己一个人决定，并把你的理由记录下来。CSA 要求社区救护员另外完成正式认可的教育。

slides.title: New for you as a PCP: watch out for
slides.body:
• Treat-and-release only with a formal protocol, training, oversight
  • “Looks fine now” ≠ safe alone tonight: who checks later?
  • Frail elders in the ED: delirium, missed meds, pressure sores
  • Scope creep: don't drift beyond protocols and licence
  • Evidence is mostly descriptive: don't overstate results
slides.say: Watch for five things. First, treat and release is only safe inside a formal protocol, with training and oversight behind it. Second, a patient who looks fine now may not be fine at midnight. Ask who will check on them, and whether they could call again. Third, remember the hidden costs of an ED trip for frail older people, and mention those risks in your handover. Fourth, watch for scope creep, duties drifting beyond your protocols and licence. Fifth, use last chapter's skills: most community paramedicine evidence is descriptive and limited in rigour, and one region's results may not carry over to yours.
slides.sayZh: 注意五件事。第一，治疗后放行只有在正式协议之内、背后有培训和监督时才安全。第二，现在看起来没事的病人，到了半夜未必没事。问问自己：谁会来看他？他还能再打电话吗？第三，记住体弱老人去急诊的隐性代价，并在交接时提到这些风险。第四，警惕范围蔓延，也就是职责漂移到你的流程和执照之外。第五，用上一章的研究技能：大多数社区院前医学证据是描述性的、严谨性有限，一个地区的结果未必能搬到你那里。

slides.title: For the BC exam
slides.body:
• Diabetic and narcotic overdose protocols both include transport
  • Hypoglycemia: BGL < 4.0 mmol/L; IV glucose is D10W only (PCP)
  • D10W: 10–25 g (100–250 mL of 10%); no D50W
  • Opioid analgesia: not on the exam (BCEHS add-on); EMRs: no IV
  • Fibrinolytics are not on the BC exam drug list
slides.say: The textbook describes treat and release for low blood sugar and opioid overdose in some systems. On the BC exam, follow the BC protocols as written: the diabetic emergencies and suspected narcotic overdose protocols both include transport. BC treats hypoglycemia at a blood glucose below four point oh. For the PCP, IV glucose is D10W only: ten to twenty-five grams, which is one hundred to two hundred fifty millilitres of the ten percent solution. There's no D50. Opioid pain relief isn't on the BC licensing exam, though BCEHS PCPs may give it after added-scope training; EMRs have no IV access; and clot-busting drugs aren't on the BC exam drug list.
slides.sayZh: 教材提到，有些系统对低血糖和阿片类过量做治疗后放行。在 BC 考试里，按 BC 流程原文做：糖尿病急症流程和疑似麻醉药过量流程都包含转运。BC 在血糖低于四点零时按低血糖处理。PCP 静脉补糖只有 D10W：十到二十五克，也就是百分之十溶液一百到二百五十毫升，没有 D50。阿片类镇痛 BC 执照考试不考（BCEHS 的 PCP 经扩展范围 Schedule 2 培训后可以给），EMR 没有静脉通路权限，溶栓药也不在 BC 考纲药物范围内。

slides.title: Three things to remember
slides.body:
1. Expanded scope = new skills; expanded role = old skills, new setting
  2. CSA types: the care, the response, or coordination differs
  3. Nontransport needs training, protocols, oversight, QA; on the exam, follow BC protocols

Next: Chapter 13, airway management and ventilation
slides.say: Let's wrap up with three things to remember. One: expanded scope means new skills and protocols; expanded role means the skills you have, used in a new setting. Two: the CSA groups programs by what's different: the care, the response, or the coordination of care. Three: deciding not to transport is risky. It needs extra training, formal protocols, medical oversight and quality assurance. On your BC exam, follow the BC protocols as written. Next class, Chapter thirteen: airway management and ventilation, where your PCP toolkit grows again. If anything was unclear, tap Ask. See you next class.
slides.sayZh: 收尾三句话。一，扩展范围是新技能和新协议；扩展角色是把已有技能用到新场景。二，CSA 按「哪里不同」给项目分类：照护不同、响应不同，或协调照护。三，决定不转运是有风险的，需要额外培训、正式协议、医疗监督和质量保证。在 BC 考试中，按 BC 流程原文做。下节课进入第十三章：气道管理与通气，你的 PCP 工具箱会再一次扩充。有不懂的点「Ask」。下节课见。
